title: Gate throughput: gate speed (F5:T7) and gate pass rate (F5:T9) to PASS
goal: Bring self-scorecard cells F5:T7 and F5:T9 to PASS without relaxing a threshold or a definition and without moving any node out of the pull-request lane. Baseline over the 30 days to main 92526921 (355 counted pull_request runs): harness_performance median 710 s against a target below 600 s (p95 1059 s, already passing), with test:cli 58% of job time because the check runner executes nodes one at a time; harness_green_main 86.8% against a target of at least 95%, with 47 failures of which 33 are real defects, 13 main-moved blocks, and 1 infrastructure (#247). Owner decisions D1 to D5 of 2026-10-07 (decisions.md): in-runner parallel workers first and sharding only if still above 600 s, auto-update branch, a pre-push preflight mandatory for agents and opt-in for humans, keep the F5:T9 definition, and ship 2.3.0 when both cells pass.

owner_effects.description: Enable the auto-update branch repository setting with the rebase update method (decision D2), after TASK-0721 records how it fits ADR-CHK-0004 and writes out the exact setting, and provide the non-GITHUB_TOKEN credential the TASK-0726 rebase-update workflow uses. The setting alone updates no pull request; TASK-0726 is the update mechanism. OE-01 is not used: the campaign policy reserves it for a merge queue, which D2 did not choose, so serialized admission stays in force.
Publish 2.3.0 (decision D5) once harness_performance and harness_green_main both read PASS over their post-change windows, from an exact candidate under a separately authorized release.

rounds.title: Gate speed (F5:T7)
rounds.goal: The pull-request gate median falls below 600 s without dropping any planned node: the check runner executes independent plan nodes on a bounded worker pool under ADR-CHK-0007, with scheduling declarations in test-task-exclusivity.json and never in test-tasks.json so the package-owned verifier and release export are unaffected (T1), test:cli is sharded across two jobs behind the single required check only if the median is still at or above 600 s afterwards (T2, conditional on D1), and the check-result cache persists across CI runs keyed by task input digest with the protected-namespace recapture rule kept (T3). Accepted when harness_performance over the post-change window of decisions.md reads a median below 600 s and every window run executed or accounted for its whole plan. Expected median about 345-430 s against the 710 s baseline.

waves.title: Exclusivity declaration schema and a closed descriptor schema

tasks.title: Define the test-task-exclusivity schema and close the test task descriptor schema
deliverables: law/schemas/test-task-exclusivity.schema.json is the closed schema of test-task-exclusivity.json under ADR-CHK-0007 rule 5: schemaVersion 1.0.0 and a nodes map from descriptor nodeId to a declaration with optional exclusive and shared arrays of distinct keys matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$, additionalProperties false at every level, admitted to the runtime roster with its counts re-pinned.

law/schemas/test-task-descriptor.schema.json is closed at the top level and on each task (additionalProperties false), every committed descriptor still validates, and a misspelled task property or a scheduling field placed in the descriptor is refused; contract tests cover both schemas.

tasks.title: Execute independent check plan nodes on a bounded worker pool under ADR-CHK-0007
deliverables: The check runner schedules plan nodes on a pool of at most W workers by rules 1 to 10 of ADR-CHK-0007: dependency readiness, plan-order admission, conflict serialization from test-task-exclusivity.json (exclusive against either list, undeclared against every node) and from overlapping output paths and a shared DEVAI_DB_URL, plan-order report and receipt assembly, unchanged per-task timeouts, and no cancellation on failure.

check --run accepts --task-workers <n>, reads DEVAI_CHECK_TASK_WORKERS, defaults to min(4, availableParallelism()), refuses values outside 1..16 with CHECK_RUNNER_WORKERS before any node starts, and runs --rc, --release-intent, and protected execution sequentially; docs/reference/error-codes.md is regenerated for the new code.

test-task-exclusivity.json declares the framework nodes and validates against law/schemas/test-task-exclusivity.schema.json; the runner refuses a file that fails the schema or names an undeclared node; test-tasks.json is unchanged; docs/adopters/test-tasks.md documents the file and the rules; tests cover IA-001 to IA-008 of ADR-CHK-0007 with an injected executor.

waves.title: Shard test:cli behind the single required check (D1 fallback)

tasks.title: Shard test:cli across two jobs behind the single required check, only if the post-T1 median is still at or above 600 s
deliverables: Started only when harness_performance over the window after TASK-0712 still reads a median at or above 600 s (decision D1); otherwise the task is cancelled with that reading recorded.

test:cli runs as two shards in two jobs, selected through vitest shard arguments in the workflow without editing test-tasks.json, whose union is exactly the test:cli node set, an aggregator job reports the single required check devai-release-gate and fails when either shard fails or is missing, and scripts/check-workflows.mjs pins the shard pair and the aggregator.

waves.title: Persist the check-result cache across CI runs

tasks.title: Persist the check-result cache across CI runs keyed by task input digest
deliverables: The pull-request workflow restores and saves the check-result cache keyed by task input digest, so a push that follows a fix reuses every unchanged PASS through the normal cache inspection.

A BLOCKED attempt is never restored as reusable (ADR-CHK-0001 IA-002), a protected-namespace node is still recaptured, and a restored cache never changes the planned node set; tests cover the three rules and scripts/check-workflows.mjs pins the cache steps.

rounds.title: Remove avoidable gate failures (F5:T9)
rounds.goal: Fewer runs fail for avoidable reasons, inside the current F5:T9 definition (D4): main-moved base-up-to-date blocks are removed only if both of these land: the auto-update branch setting with the rebase update method (T1, Owner effect OE-02), and a rebase-update trigger that rebases every open pull request when main moves, so the superseded gate run is cancelled rather than failed (T1b, TASK-0726). Real defects are caught before push by a pre-push preflight that is mandatory for agents and opt-in for humans (T2, D3), the bootstrap cache is never restored without dist (T3, #247), and the doctor-check-result-identities flake candidate is resolved (T4). Accepted when the post-change window of decisions.md, which opens only after TASK-0726 merges and OE-02 is performed, shows no main-moved failures, real-defect failures roughly halved against 33 in 355 baseline runs, and harness_green_main at or above 95%.

waves.title: Admit the rebase update-branch under ADR-CHK-0004

tasks.title: Record how the auto-update branch with the rebase method fits serialized integration
deliverables: A forward decision record amending ADR-CHK-0004, which rejected allow_update_branch because a merge commit breaks linear history: it admits the update branch only with the rebase update method, names the rebase-update trigger that TASK-0726 implements as the mechanism that updates open pull requests when main moves (the setting alone updates nothing), states that the superseded gate run is cancelled through the per-pull-request concurrency group rather than failed, and keeps strict up-to-date protection and the single required check; the catalogue is regenerated and re-pinned.
docs/dev/operations/remote-preflight-contract.md describes the update path, and the exact setting the Owner enables as OE-02 is written out for the Owner.

waves.title: Pre-push preflight in the agent contract

tasks.title: Make the pre-push preflight mandatory for agents in the contract and opt-in for humans
deliverables: AGENTS.md requires every agent session to install and keep the pre-push preflight hook (decision D3), and docs/dev/operations/remote-preflight-contract.md states what the hook runs (the commit-grammar range check and the affected check against the fetched base), how a human opts in, and that the hook never replaces the CI gate.

tasks.title: Ship an opt-in pre-push hook that runs the commit-grammar range check and the affected check
deliverables: .githooks/pre-push runs scripts/pre-push-preflight.mjs, which fetches the base, runs scripts/check-commit-range.mjs over the pushed range, and runs check --affected --run against the fetched base; it refuses the push on a failure, names the failing node, and a BLOCKED probe names the environment fix.

pnpm run hooks:install installs the hook alongside the commit-msg and pre-commit hooks without enabling it for a human who has not opted in, and an integration test covers a refused range and a clean push.

tasks.title: Never restore the pr-bootstrap cache without its compiled dist (#247)
deliverables: A pr-bootstrap cache hit whose restored tree lacks the compiled dist of any workspace package is treated as a miss and rebuilt, so the gate never dies at bootstrap with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND; scripts/check-workflows.mjs pins the guard; issue #247 is closed by the merging pull request.

tasks.title: Resolve the doctor-check-result-identities flake candidate
deliverables: The candidate is reproduced under load or shown deterministic with the evidence recorded in the pull request; a real timing dependency is removed from the test without weakening any assertion, or a product defect is recorded to the backlog under ADR-GOV-0019 for an Engineer task. No retry is added.

waves.title: Rebase-update trigger for open pull requests when main moves

tasks.title: Rebase every open pull request onto main when main moves, and cancel the superseded gate run
deliverables: .github/workflows/update-pull-request-branches.yml runs on push to main and, for every open non-draft pull request against main that is behind it, calls PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/update-branch with update_method rebase and the expected head sha. It skips a pull request whose rebase conflicts and reports it without failing the others. It uses a GitHub App or other non-GITHUB_TOKEN credential, because a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflow run and the rebased head would never be gated. The workflow holds the least permissions it needs.

The superseded gate run is cancelled rather than failed. The existing concurrency group of pull-request-checks.yml, keyed by workflow and pull request number with cancel-in-progress, already cancels an in-progress run when the rebased head arrives as a synchronize event; the task verifies this on a live pull request, records the run ids in its pull request, and changes the gate workflow only if the verification fails.
scripts/check-workflows.mjs pins the trigger, the rebase update method, the credential source, and the concurrency group, so removing any of them fails the workflow check.

rounds.title: F5:T9 measurement (deferred under D4)
rounds.goal: Only if the Owner later chooses it: redefine F5:T9 so it measures the outcome of the gate rather than developer iteration, either the final commit of each branch or merge_group runs, through a forward record on ADR-SCR-0010 and law/policy/sensor-notes/harness_green_main.md. Changes what the cell means, never what the gate checks.
rounds.disposition: Deferred by Owner decision D4 of 2026-10-07: keep the current F5:T9 definition and revisit after the R-0702 window. The round is never opened without a new Owner decision.

tasks.title: Record a redefined F5:T9 measurement if the Owner reverses D4
deliverables: Only after a new Owner decision: a forward record on ADR-SCR-0010 naming the population harness_green_main reads, the matching sensor note, and the regenerated and re-pinned catalogue.
